answer: Because the yarrow liability is logged in the delta ledger at admission, the vertex audit makes public the shared exposure and internal sponsorship is self-defeating. A sponsor carries 30% of any slash its member incurs, so vouching is a financial position rather than a courtesy. A farm must therefore place its own capital behind every sock puppet it sponsors, which is the same as paying the bond twice for each key it runs. That is 29 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
